div.head: ECf 32 D 3
div.ab: Habet eciam prata sub aeriis montibus ameno situ uirencia, in quibus fontes lucidi, per nitidos riuos leui murmure manantes, pignus suauis saporis in ripis acubantibus irrigant.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 659 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

The London compiler copies 32 D–D 6 from Geoffrey of Monmouth I 2 (Liebermann’s margin: “Galf. Monm. I 2”), printed in smaller type; Liebermann gives the passage because Lambard and later editors left it unprinted (his note d).
div.ab: It has also meadows, green in a pleasant situation beneath lofty mountains, in which clear springs, flowing with a gentle murmur in shining streams, pour a pledge of sweet savour [?] upon those lying on the banks.
